active_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.linalg.eigh for spectral contact graph analysis and targeted perturbation
active_paradigms.description: Build a contact graph from the current best solution where edges connect touching circles. Compute the graph Laplacian matrix and use scipy.linalg.eigh to find all eigenvectors. The Fiedler vector (second eigenvector) reveals the main structural direction of the contact graph. Use eigenvector centrality to identify under-constrained circles that can expand. Perturb these circles along the Fiedler vector direction to escape local optima, then re-optimize from each perturbed configuration. This is fundamentally different from random restarts because it uses the graph's spectral properties to guide the search toward promising regions.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Escape local optima by identifying structurally important circles and perturbing them in directions that respect the contact graph geometry
active_paradigms.cautions: Ensure the contact graph is connected before computing Laplacian; handle degenerate cases where multiple circles have the same position; scale perturbation magnitude appropriately (0.01-0.05)

active_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.spatial.distance.cdist for efficient contact graph construction and constraint graph analysis
active_paradigms.description: Use scipy.spatial.distance.cdist to compute all pairwise distances between circle centers in O(n²) time. Build a contact graph where edges connect circles with distance < r_i + r_j + tolerance. Analyze the constraint graph structure using graph connectivity and shortest paths to identify critical chains of constraints that limit packing density. Circles in dense constraint clusters are bottlenecks; systematically relax constraints on these circles by small amounts and re-optimize. This approach directly analyzes the constraint structure rather than relying on optimization to discover it.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Identify constraint bottlenecks through efficient distance computation and graph analysis, then target these bottlenecks for relaxation
active_paradigms.cautions: Choose appropriate tolerance for contact detection (1e-6 to 1e-4); handle numerical precision when circles are nearly touching; ensure graph connectivity is maintained after perturbations

active_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.linalg.solve for direct algebraic solution of contact constraint systems
active_paradigms.description: For optimal packings, many circles touch each other or boundaries, creating a system of algebraic equations. Identify the contact pattern (which circles touch which) from the current solution. Formulate the contact constraints as linear equations in the center coordinates (for boundary contacts) or as distance constraints (for circle-circle contacts). Use scipy.linalg.solve to directly solve the resulting linear system for exact positions that satisfy all contact constraints. This bypasses iterative optimization by directly computing the geometric solution implied by the contact pattern.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Compute exact positions that satisfy contact constraints algebraically, avoiding optimization convergence issues
active_paradigms.cautions: The system may be overconstrained or underconstrained; use least-squares (scipy.linalg.lstsq) when necessary; validate that the solution is geometrically valid (no overlaps beyond contacts)

tried_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.integrate.solve_ivp for physics-based continuous relaxation dynamics
tried_paradigms.description: Formulate circle packing as a continuous dynamical system where circles repel each other based on overlap and move toward valid configurations. Define a system of ODEs where velocity is proportional to negative gradient of a penalty function (overlap penalty + boundary penalty). Use solve_ivp with RK45 method to integrate this system from an initial configuration until convergence. This physics-based approach naturally explores configurations and can find good packings through simulated dynamics rather than direct optimization.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary sum_radii score by finding valid configurations through natural repulsion dynamics
tried_paradigms.cautions: Need to design appropriate penalty functions, may need to add damping to prevent oscillations, check convergence criteria carefully

tried_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.minimize with trust-constr method and explicit constraint gradients
tried_paradigms.description: Replace SLSQP with trust-constr method which uses interior-point algorithm with better constraint handling. Define constraints as scipy.optimize.NonlinearConstraint objects with explicit Jacobian matrices for each constraint type (containment and non-overlap). The trust-constr method maintains feasibility better and can handle tight constraints more effectively than SLSQP. Use the same initialization but with this more sophisticated constraint solver that can navigate the feasible region more carefully near the optimum.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Constraint handling near tight optima where circles are touching
tried_paradigms.cautions: trust-constr requires proper Jacobian formulation; ensure constraint gradients are computed correctly; may need different tolerance settings

tried_paradigms.idea: Reformulate non-overlap constraints using squared distances for numerical stability
tried_paradigms.description: Change constraint formulation from dist >= r_i + r_j to dist^2 >= (r_i + r_j)^2, eliminating the square root operation. This creates a differentiable quadratic constraint that is numerically more stable when circles are nearly touching. The squared formulation avoids numerical issues with square roots of small numbers and provides better gradient information for the optimizer. Keep the same optimization framework but with this mathematically equivalent but numerically superior constraint formulation.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Numerical stability when circles are nearly touching at the optimum
tried_paradigms.cautions: Ensure constraint direction is correct (>= 0); the squared formulation is only valid when distances are non-negative which they always are

tried_paradigms.idea: Use contact graph enumeration with direct geometric solution for touching circle configurations
tried_paradigms.description: Instead of relying solely on optimization, enumerate possible contact graphs (which circles touch which) based on known circle packing patterns. For each contact graph, directly solve the system of equations where touching circles satisfy dist = r_i + r_j. Use scipy.optimize.least_squares to solve this system with the contact constraints as equality constraints. This approach exploits the geometric fact that optimal packings have specific contact patterns and solves them directly rather than through inequality constraint optimization.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Finding exact touching configurations that optimization methods miss
tried_paradigms.cautions: Contact graph enumeration can be combinatorially expensive; start with plausible graphs based on hexagonal patterns; need to validate all non-contacting pairs satisfy dist >= r_i + r_j

tried_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.minimize with L-BFGS-B and penalty function approach
tried_paradigms.description: Replace explicit constraint handling with a penalty-based objective function. Instead of using SLSQP's constraint system, formulate the objective as negative sum of radii plus large penalty terms for any constraint violations (containment and overlap). This fundamentally changes the optimization landscape - L-BFGS-B can navigate differently than SLSQP, potentially escaping the current local optimum. The penalty approach smooths the constraint boundaries, allowing the optimizer to explore regions that SLSQP might reject. Use multiple restarts with varied initial configurations to find better solutions. The penalty weights should be large enough to discourage violations but not so large as to cause numerical instability.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary target_ratio by escaping local optimum through different optimization landscape
tried_paradigms.cautions: Tune penalty weights carefully - too small allows violations, too large causes numerical issues. Ensure penalty function is differentiable for L-BFGS-B. Use multiple restarts (10-20) to explore different regions of the solution space.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.minimize with COBYLA derivative-free optimization
tried_paradigms.description: Apply COBYLA (Constrained Optimization BY Linear Approximations) which uses a fundamentally different constraint handling mechanism than SLSQP. COBYLA builds linear approximations of constraints and objective without requiring gradients, using finite differences internally. This derivative-free approach can navigate the constraint landscape differently, potentially finding paths to better solutions that gradient-based methods miss. COBYLA maintains a trust region and uses simplex-based optimization. Formulate constraints explicitly (containment and non-overlap) but let COBYLA handle them through its internal linearization. Run multiple restarts with different initial configurations to maximize exploration of the solution space.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary target_ratio by exploring constraint boundaries through derivative-free optimization
tried_paradigms.cautions: COBYLA can be slower than SLSQP but may find better solutions. Set appropriate maxiter (200-400) and rhobeg (initial trust region radius, around 0.05-0.1). Ensure constraints are well-scaled for COBYLA's linear approximation approach.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.spatial.Delaunay for geometric initialization with SLSQP refinement
tried_paradigms.description: Replace Voronoi-based initialization with Delaunay triangulation, which is the dual structure to Voronoi diagrams. Delaunay triangulation provides different geometric insights about optimal circle placements - the circumcircles of Delaunay triangles naturally define empty circle regions. Use Delaunay to identify promising center locations based on triangle circumcenters, then compute initial radii from triangle circumradii or distances to edges. This geometric approach is fundamentally different from Voronoi's distance-to-vertices method and may provide better starting configurations for n=26. After Delaunay-based initialization, apply SLSQP optimization for local refinement to maximize the sum of radii while satisfying all constraints.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary target_ratio through better initial configuration that SLSQP can refine to global optimum
tried_paradigms.cautions: Delaunay triangulation requires at least 3 points - handle edge cases carefully. Some Delaunay triangles may be obtuse or degenerate. Filter out poor triangle circumcenters before using as initial centers. Ensure the final configuration has exactly 26 circles after any filtering.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.spatial.cKDTree for efficient neighbor constraint identification
tried_paradigms.description: Build a scipy.spatial.cKDTree from circle centers to efficiently query nearby circles within a radius threshold. Only generate non-overlap constraints for pairs that are actually close (within 2*max_radius), reducing from 325 constraints to ~50-80 active constraints. This dramatically improves SLSQP convergence by focusing on relevant constraints and reducing the constraint Jacobian size. The tree query uses ball_tree or kdtree with radius parameter to find all neighbors within a distance threshold.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Reduce constraint count for faster SLSQP convergence, allowing more restart iterations or better local optima exploration
tried_paradigms.cautions: Need to update the KDTree during optimization or use conservative radius estimates; ensure no constraints are missed for valid solutions

tried_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.NonlinearConstraint with trust-constr for robust constraint handling
tried_paradigms.description: Replace the manual constraint function with scipy.optimize.NonlinearConstraint objects for non-overlap constraints. Use the trust-constr method which handles nonlinear constraints more robustly than SLSQP. Define separate NonlinearConstraint for each pair of nearby circles with lb=0 (distance >= r1+r2). This uses interior-point methods with better numerical stability for the quadratic distance constraints. Combine with LinearConstraint for box constraints to leverage scipy's specialized constraint solvers.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Improve constraint satisfaction and numerical stability to reach higher sum_radii values closer to 2.635 target
tried_paradigms.cautions: trust-constr requires bounds and constraints in specific format; may need Jacobian approximation tuning; different API than minimize constraints

tried_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.spatial.distance.pdist for vectorized constraint evaluation
tried_paradigms.description: Replace the nested loop constraint computation with scipy.spatial.distance.pdist to compute all pairwise distances in a single vectorized operation. Use pdist with metric='euclidean' to get condensed distance array, then use squareform to get full matrix. This enables efficient batch constraint evaluation and gradient computation. The vectorized approach is significantly faster than nested loops and allows better numerical precision. Use the condensed form directly in constraints to avoid memory overhead.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Improve constraint evaluation speed and numerical precision, enabling more optimization iterations within timeout
tried_paradigms.cautions: pdist returns condensed array (1D), need squareform for full matrix or work with condensed format; ensure constraint indexing matches condensed format
